do.name: Noto Cathedral and its grand staircase
do.detail: The honey-toned limestone duomo tops three flights of steps above Corso Vittorio Emanuele; best in the low golden light.

do.name: Baroque balconies of Palazzo Nicolaci
do.detail: Six balconies carried on carved cherubs, lions and sea monsters, built in the 1700s by a family who made their money in tuna. The most photographed wall in the town.

do.name: Infiorata di Noto flower carpet
do.detail: The third weekend of May: a whole street laid with pictures made of flower petals, designed for weeks and placed overnight by hand.

do.name: Granita and cassata at Caffe Sicilia
do.detail: The 1892 pasticceria on Corso Vittorio Emanuele, famed for almond granita, cassata and cannoli under pastry chef Corrado Assenza.

do.name: Vendicari reserve walk and Calamosche swim
do.detail: Easy coastal paths link lagoons with flamingos and herons, an 18th century tuna fishery ruin, and the sheltered Calamosche cove.

do.name: Noto Antica ruins and Cava Carosello
do.detail: The earthquake-ruined old town 15 km uphill keeps castle and prison remains; the gorge below has a river to swim and old tanneries.
